text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports recurrent lower respiratory infections, with a recent episode of cough, mucus production, shortness of breath, and low-grade fever, now improving.
- history of present illness: the patient has had lower respiratory infections roughly every 1–2 months over the past six months, often requiring urgent care, primary care, or one emergency room visit. Symptoms last a few days to a week. Symptoms begin on days the patient unloads hay for a sibling, who does not wear a mask. No history of seasonal allergies, smoking, or smoke exposure.
- physical examination: respiratory rate 20, SpO2 99% on room air, regular heart rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops, fine rales on lung exam without wheezes, no digital clubbing. Chest x-ray shows round ground-glass opacities.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: cough, excessive mucus, shortness of breath, low-grade fever.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: oral steroid course prescribed for current symptoms (dosage N/A).
- follow-up instructions: chest CT of the lungs and pulmonary function test ordered; avoid hay exposure, or wear a respirator when handling hay if avoidance is not possible.
